title: US finalises $38M CHIPS award for silicon quantum company Diraq
excerpt: Diraq has finalised an award of up to $38mn from the US Commerce Department's CHIPS programme to build and test its silicon quantum chips in the US.
content_html:
Six months after Washington promised Diraq money, the contract was signed. The quantum computing company said today that the US Commerce Department has finalised its award of up to $38M under the CHIPS programme.

The money pays for making and testing Diraq’s quantum chips on American soil, and for designing the large processing units a useful quantum computer will need.

It came out of a roughly $2bn CHIPS Act quantum round, the same one that promised PsiQuantum $100mn. Earlier reports said Washington takes small, non-controlling stakes in the companies it backs.

“Quantum computing will be a core technology of the next decade,” said Andrew Dzurak, Diraq’s founder and CEO, in a statement.

Diraq’s pitch is that its qubits are made like ordinary chips. Its silicon spin qubits use the same processes and materials as the processors in phones and laptops, so standard foundries can produce them.

The company is aiming for 150,000 physical qubits supporting up to 1,000 error-corrected ones by 2029. Two years later it wants millions, in systems the size of about four server racks.

The award crowns a year in which most things have gone Diraq’s way. In October it reached the final stage of DARPA’s quantum benchmarking programme, bringing an initial $51mn and up to $300mn more if its machines prove commercially useful by 2033.

Before the year is out, the company also wants a silicon spin machine running inside an Equinix data centre in Sydney. No computer of its kind has run in a commercial facility before.

Diraq began in Sydney in 2022 as a University of New South Wales spinout. It now has more than 130 people, with US sites in Palo Alto, Chicago, Los Angeles, and Albuquerque. Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund holds a A$20mn stake.

Diraq is hardly alone in drawing state money into quantum. France has bet €500mn on its national champions, the EU is preparing its own quantum push, and Washington is using CHIPS money to pull production onto American soil.
